author: /root/memory_red
body: Proposed bounded grammar before test drafting: accept only a closed two-binder Nat telescope with exact outer order `exists(w), forall(x)` or `forall(x), exists(w)`, unique source binder IDs, and one identical predicate-shaped body over exactly those two variables; binders carry no extra local context, assumptions remain empty, and both contract telescopes must exactly match their interpretation IDs/types/order. The witnessDependencies entry must name w and its allowedBinderIds must reflect lexical scope: no x for ∃w∀x; x for ∀x∃w. A metadata/formula conflict rejects; unsupported sorts, premises, extra binders, extra context, nonmatching predicate shape, or ambiguous witness roles return unsupported. Goal construction uses both `lower_formula` outputs verbatim under their original quantifier orders, planning implication/counterexample obligations without commuting quantifiers. The source-bound plan must still resolve each interpretation and its own source-map/correspondence closure through the ordinary planner. I will test the natural strictness instance P(w,x): x ≤ w using actual Nat AST constructors and avoid claiming semantic separation absent checked evidence.

author: /root/memory_audit
body: Concrete permission trap for the proposed exact pair: the left telescope exists(w), forall(x) requires its known witnessDependencies[w].allowedBinderIds=[]; the right telescope forall(x), exists(w) requires allowedBinderIds=[x] under validate_contract’s earlier-forall rule. Thus full metadata-row equality across readings is impossible for the very contrast being tested. Read “agree exactly” as same witness binder identity/state and exact per-side agreement with its own AST/order, while comparing all non-permission metadata exactly. Do not canonicalize/sort telescopes: source telescope must remain [w,x] on one side and [x,w] on the other; require the same unique role IDs and exact body references by those IDs. If metadata conflicts with a recognized AST, reject; if extra/malformed/dependent domains, unknown symbols, extra role binders, or external context falls outside the profile, return unsupported before generating goals. Keep both generated goals in each original quantifier order and only classify separation after the exact P ∧ ¬Q obligation completes, replays, and passes trust; failed/missing terms remain unresolved. Quantifier implication asymmetry is real: over Nat, ∃w∀x P implies ∀x∃w P; the converse needs a checked separation, never a syntactic verdict. Source binding should require both interpretation/contract/correspondence owners, same exact closed selected slice/object map/environment, and current quote/source verification so a right-formula proof is not attributed to an unrelated left-source context.

Do not demand equality of permission arrays across sides or canonicalize telescopes. Use P(w,x): x ≤ w only if the AST/type checker support stays exact; otherwise disclose unsupported lowering. Keep final separation status tied to completed/replayed/trusted exact goals, not syntax.

author: /root/application_probe_green
body:
Read contract719, OpenSpec probe design/spec/tasks, docs/PROOF_CONTRACTS.md, public API/CLI/worker/pair/native replay, and constant-uniformity implementation. Recommended smallest v1 grammar: exactly two Nat binders and one unchanged body application P(w,x), with P’s actual symbol mapping Nat→Nat→Prop. Admit only ∃w:Nat, ∀x:Nat, P(w,x) and ∀x:Nat, ∃w:Nat, P(w,x); arbitrary actual binder and symbol IDs, but the same role IDs and typed P mapping on both sides. No extra binders, arithmetic, conjunction, opaque nodes, assumptions, non-Nat sorts, dependent domains, open local contexts, or object-map transport. This makes the task’s witness-choice distinction precise without importing estimate-specific M/F/N/mul/add syntax. Preserve both complete formulas; never normalize/reorder quantifiers. Generate right-full-reading IFF actual plus the complete selected direction between left/right; for a discrepancy use weak→strong counterexample, while strong→weak is the logical control implication. Derive roles from AST only, then require the telescope to match exact binder IDs/order/types/quantifiers. Require one known witnessDependencies row anchored at w with [] permissions for ∃w∀x or [x] for ∀x∃w. Known anchor/order/permission/telescope conflicts should reject; unknown relevant witness metadata should stay unsupported. Validate via proof_contracts.validate_contract, and require non-witness context/endpoint/conclusion/assumption/feature records to match across sides. Do not infer the AST from any feature summary.

Reuse existing public request, plan/check CLI, native exact-owner/correspondence regeneration, common result/goal schema, _planned_input_size, validate_contract, lower_formula, and closed shared-slice checks. The current constant AST helper is too specialized to reuse as a parser: factor only generic ordered binder/goal/bounds helpers or add a separate lazily imported witness matcher behind template_result to avoid import cycles. Keep PROFILE_DIGEST/native payload shape unchanged; profile descriptor gains implemented=true for current witness v1, and no new public request fields are needed. Source acceptance needs two distinct quote/source-map/contract/correspondence owners in one complete closed slice, actual source preparation excluding parent theorem, and both actual completion/replay/trust checks for formal-reading and probe; weak/weak from distinct owners is a control. Retain missing/failed terms as unresolved. Ordinary inspect/SQLite must recompute identical v1 goals.

Compatibility risk: flipping witness-dependence-v1 from generic unsupported may change recomputation for archived unsupported artifacts, whose old result used scope closed-nat-regularity-v1 and residual unsupported-template-family. Preserve exact old fallback bytes for nonmatching AST inputs if possible and add replay coverage; valid previously unsupported witness inputs have no old planned goals. Docs/PROOF_CONTRACTS currently says the other three consumers are unsupported and would need a witness section; OpenSpec currently has only a generic uniformity scenario and task1.1 remains open until all five families. Existing callers are application_probe_profile, validate_template, template_result→derive_probe_result→native artifact/inspect replay, and plan/check-probe; don’t fork API/CLI. No code/tests/Lean/source runs were performed.

author: /root/memory_audit
body: One additional metadata edge to pin in the v2 contract/tests: `features.constantDependencies` is mandatory and may optionally anchor at the same sole existential w. When that constant row and the witness row are both known, `proof_contracts._constant_witness_coherence` requires identical allowedBinderIds within each side. Therefore a valid anchored-known row also has [] on ∃w∀x and [x] on ∀x∃w. Pair comparison that requires exact equality of the entire “non-witness feature record” will reject this otherwise AST-consistent pair, even if witnessDependencies itself is handled correctly. Safest narrow profile: require constantDependencies to be unknown and identical on both sides, with only witnessDependencies modeling the varying permission; or explicitly treat the allowedBinderIds on a constantDependencies row anchored to w as another AST-derived permission exception (same binder/state/reason, per-side scope checks). Please add one recognized-AST test for this branch so it cannot be ambiguously classified unsupported. I confirmed validate_contract permits an unanchored unknown constantDependencies row and enforces cross-feature coherence when both are known.
